workflow.name: Authorization and Business Logic Abuse v2
workflow.description: Scope-aware actor-resource-action mapping, independent authorization and workflow abuse fan-out, root-cause deduplication, adversarial verification, stateful PoC, eligibility gating, and ranking. Import-valid v2.2: globally unique stage output keys, one consume-all dedup boundary, immutable program extras after dedup, deterministic mapping, high-priority PoC gating, and explicit Web3 fork inputs.

steps.name: Freeze program scope contract
Map actor-resource-action and workflow boundaries
steps.content:
Map every in-scope production operation where an external actor reads protected data, mutates state, spends value/quota, changes identity/privilege, crosses a tenant, invokes administration, or advances a sensitive workflow. Prove registration. For each distinct actor-resource-action boundary, trace how subject, tenant, object, role, and workflow state are derived through middleware, policy helpers, services, queues, and downstream calls. Record the least-privileged actor, controlled IDs/fields, intended authorization and state invariants, enforcement traces, terminal effect, and matching accepted-impact candidates. No vulnerabilities.

Use deterministic enumeration before reasoning: ripgrep plus language-aware AST/compiler tooling when available. Perform {{extra.repeat_runs}} independent enumeration passes when supplied (default: 2), compare their coverage, and record any coverage gap.

steps.name: Hypotheses A: identity, object, tenant, privilege
steps.content: Fresh-context analysis of boundary {{surface_boundary_label}} at {{surface_entrypoint_file_path}}:{{surface_entrypoint_line}}. Generate one hypothesis per precise horizontal/vertical privilege change, cross-tenant substitution, IDOR/BOLA, confused deputy, mass assignment, subject/object mismatch, alternate endpoint, stale authorization, role escalation, canonicalization collision, or downstream authorization gap. Each record must name the changed attacker field/sequence, broken invariant, exact suspected guard gap, locations, preconditions, accepted impact, candidate guards, and strongest falsification target.

steps.name: Hypotheses B: state machine and multi-request abuse
steps.content: Independently analyze boundary {{surface_boundary_label}} with fresh context. Generate one hypothesis per precise step skip, replay, duplicate, reordering, race, TOCTOU, partial failure, retry/idempotency error, negative/boundary value, quota/accounting drift, cancellation/rollback, or cross-channel workflow abuse. Require a concrete attacker sequence, reachable state prerequisites, broken invariant, faulty location, terminal security effect, accepted-impact candidate, and falsification target. No generic checklist.

steps.name: Deduplicate authorization root causes
steps.content: Review {{multi_output_depth_2}} and cluster by missing/faulty enforcement operation, attacker primitive, broken authorization/state invariant, terminal effect, and fix. Merge endpoint/payload/state variants of the same root bug. Create stable fingerprints; retain alternate trigger paths, conflicts, and gaps. Discard UI-only restrictions, generic hardening, self-only actions without security effect, and unsupported impact.

steps.name: Independent authorization abuse verification
steps.content: As a new verifier, try to disprove {{dedup_canonical_hypothesis_id}}. Reconstruct authentication -> subject/tenant derivation -> object loading -> authorization -> state transition -> terminal effect across middleware, services, jobs, and downstream checks. Prove control over each identifier, field, timing, and prerequisite state. Inspect ownership, tenancy, policy caching, idempotency, database constraints, isolation/locking, transactions, rollback, feature flags, and alternate guards. supported requires a complete production path and concrete cross-boundary or security-sensitive effect; otherwise falsified/blocked. Produce a minimal isolated multi-account reproduction plan.

steps.name: Stateful multi-account PoC gate
steps.content:
For supported candidates, reproduce in an authorized isolated environment with the smallest stateful sequence and at least two principals/tenants when relevant. Capture identities/roles, object ownership, requests/events, before/after state, response and downstream effect. Prefer an integration/regression test and repeat the decisive sequence. Respect {{extra.authorized_test_constraints}}. Set PoC verdict and preserve commands, evidence, artifacts, minimal reproduction, and assumptions.

Cost gate: if {{dedup_triage_priority}} is not `high`, do not build or run a harness. Return poc_verdict=`skipped_by_priority` with the reason. For smart-contract candidates, use {{extra.fork_rpc_url}} and {{extra.fork_block}} when supplied.

steps.name: Apply program eligibility gate
steps.content:
Apply the immutable program scope contract to this technically verified candidate.
Program evidence is read directly from immutable extras after dedup: snapshot={{extra.program_rules_snapshot}}; checked_at={{extra.program_rules_checked_at}}; URL={{extra.bug_bounty_url}}; deployment={{extra.deployment_evidence}}; known_issues={{extra.known_issues_snapshot}}; testing_constraints={{extra.authorized_test_constraints}}.
Candidate: {{dedup_canonical_summary}}. Root cause: {{dedup_canonical_root_cause}} at {{dedup_canonical_location}}.
Technical verdict: {{verify_technical_verdict}}. Production reachability: {{verify_production_reachability}}.
Observed effect: {{poc_observed_effect}}. Reproduction verdict: {{poc_poc_verdict}}. Reproduction evidence: {{poc_poc_evidence}}.

Set eligibility_verdict=eligible only when the exact affected asset is in scope, the observed effect matches a named accepted impact, no exclusion or known-issue rule controls, and required deployment facts are evidenced. Use ineligible for a controlling exclusion or absent impact; use blocked for missing program/deployment facts. Assign severity only from the supplied program language and measured impact. Do not use popularity, theoretical TVL, scanner confidence, or remembered platform conventions.

steps.name: Report verified authorization finding
